column3: Consent Management — Obtain free specific informed unconditional and unambiguous consent; limited to data necessary for specified purpose
column7: ISO 27001 does not address consent lifecycle. Build consent management platform with purpose-bound granularity immutable audit trail and Consent Manager interoperability (S.6(7)-(9)). Withdrawal must be possible "with the ease of doing so being comparable to the ease with which such consent was given" (S.6(4)).

column7: ISO 27001's A.5.12 requires data classification by confidentiality/integrity/availability. Extend schema to include "personal_data_dpdpa" tier with purpose-bound access controls and retention policies.

column7: A.5.14 covers secure transfer but not accuracy obligations. Implement data quality checks validation rules and correction workflows. Add accuracy attestation to data transfer protocols.

column3: Reasonable Security Safeguards — Protect personal data by taking reasonable security safeguards to prevent breach
column7: ISO 27001's core purpose aligns directly with this. Your certified ISMS provides strong evidence of "reasonable safeguards." Ensure controls are risk-proportionate to volume/sensitivity of personal data and check them against the Rule 6(1) minimum list (encryption/masking/tokens; access control; logs and monitoring; backups; one-year log retention under 6(1)(e); processor contract clauses).

column3: Breach Notification — Notify Data Protection Board AND affected Data Principals of personal data breaches in prescribed form/manner
column5: Incident management planning and preparation; Response to information security incidents
column7: A.5.24/A.5.26 cover incident management but not regulatory notification. Extend incident response playbook with DPDPA branch: per Rule 7: initial intimation to the Board (7(2)(a)) and each affected Data Principal (7(1)) without delay; then the detailed Board report within 72 hours of awareness (7(2)(b)) extendable on written request.

column3: Data Erasure on Purpose Completion — Erase personal data upon consent withdrawal OR when purpose no longer served (whichever earlier) unless legal retention required
column7: A.8.10 covers secure deletion but not DPDPA-specific triggers. Implement automated erasure evaluation: (1) consent withdrawal (2) purpose completion per S.8(8) inactivity period. Cascade to backups and Data Processors (S.8(7)(b)). Respect the Rule 8(3) one-year minimum retention of personal data traffic data and processing logs.

column3: Right to Correction and Erasure — Data Principal can request correction completion updating erasure of personal data
column7: A.8.10 provides deletion mechanism but not request handling. Build DSAR (Data Subject Access Request) API for correction and erasure requests. Respond within prescribed timelines. Maintain audit log.

column3: Purpose Expiry Definition — Purpose deemed no longer served if Data Principal has not approached for performance AND not exercised rights for prescribed period
column7: ISO 27001 has no purpose expiry calculation. Implement automated purpose expiry evaluation based on last interaction date + prescribed period per Data Fiduciary class and purpose. Rule 8(1) and the Third Schedule prescribe 3 years only for e-commerce entities and social media intermediaries with 2 crore+ registered users and online gaming intermediaries with 50 lakh+; warn the Data Principal 48 hours before erasure (Rule 8(2)).
